projects.readme: # SceneTrace 3D ### Computer Vision · Gaussian Splatting · Forensic & Historical Reconstruction Research [Live review demo](https://scenetrace-3d-vams2krish.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site) · [Operations and security boundaries](docs/OPERATIONS.md) · [Dependency attribution](docs/THIRD_PARTY.md) · [Measured experiments](docs/experiments/sparse-input.json) **SceneTrace 3D turns overlapping photos or video frames into a source-linked 3D research artifact.** Inventory original media, select derivatives, estimate cameras with COLMAP, fit Gaussian colors, inspect the result in a WebGL viewer, separate observations from hypotheses, and export review records. > **Release v0.2.0: working research demo and local single-user service.** The hosted Site is a private-to-owner static review demo. Actual media reconstruction runs through the local Python service. This is not a certified forensic tool or a production-ready multiuser service. No real case data is published here. ![SceneTrace workbench running locally](docs/showcase/01-workbench.jpg) *Actual application screenshot with a procedural synthetic Gaussian room. This is not a real scene or a photorealistic reconstruction benchmark.* ## Product showcases ### Source inventory and provenance Choose local media, compute SHA-256 hashes, and submit explicitly to the local worker. Originals remain separate from selected image derivatives. ![Local media inventory with real calculated source hashes](docs/showcase/04-source-inventory.jpg) ### Validation with held-out comparisons Inspect the synthetic observation and fitted Gaussian render side by side, read the actual metrics, and keep evaluation caveats visible. ![Held-out appearance comparison and limitations](docs/showcase/02-validation.jpg) ### Separate observation and hypothesis layers Notes reference specific source views and persist per scene in browser storage. Both layers are included in the review JSON export. ![Observation and hypothesis notes in the running product](docs/showcase/03-review-notes.jpg) ### Actual browser-to-COLMAP output The browser uploaded nine synthetic textured captures, the local worker recovered cameras and sparse geometry, fitted Gaussian colors, and returned this navigable artifact. The sparse appearance is an actual output limitation, not concealed by substituting the synthetic room. ![Completed local COLMAP reconstruction from browser-submitted captures](docs/showcase/05-colmap-result.jpg) ### Responsive review All showcase images above are screenshots of the running product. The [original AI-generated concept banner](docs/assets/scenetrace-concept.png) is retained separately with its [prompt and disclosure](docs/illustration-prompt.md); it is not a product result. ## What works today | Capability | Implemented behavior | | --- | --- | | Source inventory | SHA-256, source-byte counts, stable source IDs, decode failure records | | Frame preparation | JPEG/PNG/WebP; OpenCV video extraction; interval and candidate budget; normalized PNG derivatives | | Selection decisions | Laplacian sharpness heuristic and exact normalized-pixel duplicate detection, recorded per candidate | | Camera recovery | CPU PyCOLMAP feature extraction, exhaustive matching, incremental mapping, camera export | | Gaussian reconstruction | Original CPU backend with fixed isotropic geometry/scales/opacity and bounded least-squares RGB fitting | | Synthetic evaluation | Seeded 1,789-Gaussian room, six training views and two held-out views, PSNR and train MSE | | Review UI | Orbit/zoom, point mode, camera navigation, source hashes, validation comparisons, responsive layout | | Review notes | Source-linked observations and hypotheses; scene-specific browser persistence; removal and export | | Local job service | One active subprocess, ten-minute deadline, persisted success/failure, review ZIP export | | Hosted demo | Static deployment with committed synthetic artifacts, local hashing, JSON import, notes and exports | | Verification | Eight automated tests, live browser upload-to-result run, live duplicate-input failure check, CI workflow | ## Run the demo locally Use **Python 3.12** for the tested environment. No OpenAI key, external AI API, GPU, COLMAP executable, Node dependency installation, or FFmpeg executable is required. PyCOLMAP and OpenCV wheels supply the used functionality. ```powershell git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-SceneTrace-3D.git cd DL-SceneTrace-3D python -m venv .venv .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-lock.txt .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install --no-deps -e . .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli serve ``` Open **http://127.0.0.1:8765/**. On Linux/macOS, replace `.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe` with `.venv/bin/python`. 1. Explore the synthetic room, select source thumbnails, and compare held-out views in **Validation**. 2. Add an observation and a hypothesis in **Review notes**, reload, and export the review JSON. 3. In **Source inventory**, choose 4–40 overlapping photos or a video. Up to 40 files and 90 MiB of source bytes are accepted by the local UI. 4. Submit **Run local reconstruction**. The worker requires at least four distinct, sufficiently sharp derivative views. Registration can fail when overlap or texture is inadequate. 5. Inspect the returned scene, source records, and limitations. Download the worker review bundle. Failed jobs expose their reason instead of substituting a demo scene. The hosted Site runs the review functions without a Python server. Its reconstruction control remains unavailable; it does not upload files or run COLMAP in the cloud. Scene JSON can be imported there, but its relative source-image links require the local service or a corresponding artifact directory; imported JSON does not embed source media. This release accepts its own schema, not arbitrary `.ply` or `.splat` files. ## Reproduce the complete synthetic photo pipeline ```powershell # Make perspective photographs of textured synthetic 3D patches. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/generate_sfm_fixture.py data/sfm-input # Inventory only, with explicit derivative selection parameters. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli inventory data/sfm-input data/inventory-run --max-frames 40 # Recover cameras and geometry from pixels, then fit Gaussian RGB. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli reconstruct data/sfm-input data/reconstruction-run # Independently regenerate the supplied-camera appearance-fitting demo. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m scenetrace.cli demo data/gaussian-demo-run # Controlled 4/6/9-view experiment; work directory must be new. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/sparse_experiment.py --work data/experiment-new # With the local server running: verify a real subprocess failure and queue release. .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/verify_local_api.py .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q ``` Outputs are never silently overwritten by the inventory/reconstruction commands; choose a new output directory for reruns. The Gaussian demo command regenerates its explicitly selected demo destination. CLI inventory supports `--interval` in seconds and `--max-frames` (candidate budget, including rejected candidates). ## Measured output ### Gaussian optimizer experiment | Measurement | Observed result | | --- | --- | | Scene | Procedural archive room; seed 17 | | Gaussians | 1,789 | | Training / held-out views | 6 / 2 | | Training MSE before → after | 0.00379316 → 0.00000158 | | Mean held-out PSNR | 56.61 dB | | RGB solver success | All three channels | See [committed metrics](demo/dist/sample/metrics.json), [scene artifact](demo/dist/sample/scene.json), and [generator](scenetrace/demo.py). **Interpretation:** cameras, geometry, scale, and opacity are supplied by the synthetic generator. Only colors are fitted. The same renderer generates and evaluates observations; the score is an optimizer smoke test and does not predict real-scene reconstruction quality. ### Camera recovery from rendered photographs These experiments use a separate seed-21 textured 3D-patch fixture. Camera poses are estimated from the image pixels through COLMAP; ground-truth poses are not passed to reconstruction. | Input captures | Cameras registered | Triangulated points | Train MSE after RGB fit | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 4 | 4 | 4,934 | 0.04153 | | 6 | 6 | 7,444 | 0.03261 | | 9 | 7 | 8,521 | 0.02922 | The nine-view run excludes two images from both SfM and fitting. Independent localization of those held-out images is not implemented, so no held-out score is claimed for these reconstructions. Four/six-view runs use all selected views. The [full report](docs/experiments/sparse-input.json) includes runtime and similarity-aligned camera-center diagnostics. Alignment is fitted to the same training camera centers; it is not independent geometry validation. Timings depend on the host and are not throughput claims. A separate live browser run also registered seven cameras from nine uploaded synthetic images and produced a downloadable worker bundle. [Live duplicate-media failure report](docs/experiments/api-failure.json) verifies that inadequate distinct views fail explicitly and release the worker slot. ## How reconstruction works ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Original photos or videos] --> B[SHA-256 inventory] B --> C[Frame derivatives and quality decisions] C --> D[CPU COLMAP camera and sparse point recovery] D --> E[Fixed isotropic Gaussian initialization] E --> F[Bounded least-squares RGB fitting] F --> G[Scene JSON and validation records] G --> H[WebGL review and source-linked notes] H --> I[Review JSON or worker ZIP] ``` The CPU backend projects Gaussian centers, approximates screen-space isotropic footprints, sorts by depth, and composites front to back. With positions, scales, and opacity fixed, pixel color is linear in Gaussian RGB, so bounded sparse least squares can fit appearance without a neural network or CUDA. A small color prior stabilizes weakly observed splats. It does **not** optimize Gaussian positions, full covariance, opacity, spherical harmonics, or adaptive densification. The WebGL preview uses depth-sorted point sprites and is approximate; CPU render outputs are used for reported evaluation. Photo reconstruction is capped at 1,600 splats and fitted at 96×96, so it is a small research baseline with visibly incomplete detail. ## Is it ML, DL, or Generative AI? The implemented release is **computer vision + numerical optimization + differentiable-rendering-inspired Gaussian splatting**. It contains no trained deep neural network, pretrained weights, LLM, or Generative AI scene completion. The `DL-SceneTrace-3D` repository name preserves the original proposed DL direction; **DL extensions remain roadmap work**. Original 3D Gaussian Splatting optimizes an explicit scene representation and does not inherently require a deep network. Novel-view synthesis is not evidence of hidden geometry or event history. Any future learned depth/features or generative hypothesis layers must be identified and evaluated separately. ## Data, provenance, and limits - Hashes detect changes in bytes; they do not authenticate the source or establish chain of custody. - Source media stays separate from normalized derivatives. Available source content is not silently altered. - Sharpness and coverage diagnostics are heuristics, not calibrated correctness probabilities. - Static scene capture cannot establish event sequence, intent, identity, or what happened outside observed areas. - Real-world scale and measurement accuracy require independent references. Gaussian appearance is not a validated physical surface or watertight mesh. - Moving objects, reflective surfaces, weak texture, and inconsistent capture times can invalidate reconstruction assumptions. - Do not publish actual case files or identifying metadata. `data/`, media outputs, local secrets, and model files are ignored by Git. - The local worker ZIP contains review JSON and submitted-name mapping; originals, derivative images, worker logs, and COLMAP binary files stay in the local job directory. - Browser notes are local, removable, and exportable; this is not a tamper-evident evidence management system. Read [OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md) for implemented controls, recovery, retention, and production release gates. The loopback service must not be exposed as a public multiuser backend. ## Roadmap and release boundary - [x] Source inventory and original-media hashing. - [x] Still/video derivative selection with recorded blur and duplicate decisions. - [x] Reproducible CPU COLMAP integration and failure reporting. - [x] Original license-independent CPU Gaussian RGB baseline and staged synthetic demo. - [x] Held-out appearance evaluation for supplied synthetic cameras. - [x] Source-linked WebGL review, separate hypothesis notes, and exports. - [x] Controlled sparse-input experiments on synthetic photographs. - [x] Automated checks, live browser flow, real screenshots, and hosted review demo. - [ ] Full anisotropic Gaussian geometry/opacity optimization and densification. - [ ] Independent held-out camera localization for uploaded scenes. - [ ] Surveyed scale, independent geometry evaluation, and calibrated uncertainty. - [ ] Optional learned features/depth with explicit DL evaluation. - [ ] Persistent authenticated multiuser case storage, sandboxed GPU workers, access auditing, backups, and retention controls. - [ ] Independent security/accessibility review and real-data performance evaluation. - [ ] Qualified forensic review before operational or evidentiary use. ## Repository map ```text scenetrace/ Media inventory, COLMAP pipeline, Gaussian backend, CLI, API scripts/ Synthetic generators, sparse experiment, live failure check tests/ Integrity, media, numerical, API, and export tests demo/dist/ Dependency-free hosted/browser application and sample artifacts demo/.openai/ Sites hosting identity and static deployment configuration docs/showcase/ Six screenshots of the running application docs/experiments/ Actual sparse-input results and live failure report docs/OPERATIONS.md Local service boundaries and production release gates requirements-lock.txt Exact tested Python dependency versions .github/workflows/ CI checks for code and tests ``` ## Research foundations - Kerbl, Kopanas, Leimkühler, and Drettakis (2023), [3D Gaussian Splatting for Real-Time Radiance Field Rendering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.04079). - [COLMAP tutorial](https://colmap.github.io/tutorial.html) and [PyCOLMAP documentation](https://colmap.github.io/pycolmap/index.html). - projects.readme: # SignBridge — Deep Learning Accessibility Studio **Gesture → captions & speech · Speech/text → illustrative avatar** A working browser demo that explores two-way accessible communication with on-device deep learning, editable captions, and a 3D companion named Ari. **[Open the live demo](https://signbridge-gesture-lab.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site)** · Hosted privately through Sites; sign in with the owning account. The source repository remains public. > **Release scope:** deployable research demo, not a production-ready sign-language interpreter. This version recognizes **seven isolated hand gestures** and maps a bounded set of English phrases to illustrative avatar poses. It does not translate ASL, continuous signing, or arbitrary sentences. No translation-accuracy claim is made. ## Product showcases These are actual screenshots of the implemented application. The original AI-generated cover remains in [concept artwork](docs/artwork.md). ### 1. The studio Permission-based camera input, local vision, editable captions, speech controls, and a 3D avatar in one workspace. ![SignBridge studio with camera controls, captions, avatar and seven-gesture library](docs/showcase/01-studio.png) ### 2. Real model recognition The sample button runs the actual MediaPipe model on an attributed test photograph. A thumb-up classification proposes “Yes” for review. The confidence shown is a model score, not measured accuracy; the inference time is specific to the test device and excludes capture, holding, review, and speech. ![Actual thumb-up sample recognition with landmarks, model score and editable Yes caption](docs/showcase/02-recognition.png) ### 3. Text to avatar “Peace” selects the illustrative Victory pose. The avatar has articulated fingers, a procedural upper body, adjustable idle motion, and decorative mouth movement during speech. These motions are not linguist-validated sign-language animations. ![Speech and text input driving the Victory gesture on the Ari avatar](docs/showcase/03-avatar.png) ### 4. The supported gesture library Each category includes a pose hint, chosen communication intent, and avatar preview. The chosen phrases are demo conventions, not an ASL dictionary. ![Seven supported gesture categories with pose instructions and preview controls](docs/showcase/04-library.png) ### 5. Mobile layout The studio stacks its input and output panels on smaller screens, with the same consent, fallback, and caption controls. Browser support for camera, speech recognition, and WebGL varies; physical mobile-device validation remains pending. ## What works now | Capability | Implementation and boundary | | --- | --- | | Live gesture recognition | Self-hosted MediaPipe neural model, CPU inference in a browser worker, one hand at a time | | Temporal proposal filtering | Default 70% model-score threshold, 650 ms confident camera hold, release-based repeat suppression | | Sample without camera | Real inference on Google's attributed thumb-up test photo; no synthetic prediction | | Caption review | Editable caption, user-triggered text-to-speech, stop speaking, voice selection | | Speech input | Optional browser speech recognition with separate consent and editable transcript | | Text/speech to avatar | Whole-phrase matching against seven supported intents; unsupported text remains visible | | Avatar | Procedural Three.js character with articulated fingers and seven illustrative static gesture poses | | Privacy controls | No application recording, upload, analytics, backend, or persistent conversation storage | | Session history | Confirmed speech and avatar messages in memory, capped at 20; clear session also stops devices | | Accessibility | Semantic controls, native modal dialogs, visible focus, live status, reduced-motion option, text fallback | | Evaluation tooling | Local image-manifest harness with declared signer separation, duplicate detection, confusion matrix and latency | | Verification | Unit tests, browser integration tests, accessibility scan, production build, dependency audit, GitHub Actions workflow | Browser speech recognition may send audio to its provider. TTS voices can be local or remote; local voices are labeled. Camera processing stays on the device. Hiding the page, switching the app view/direction, or clearing the session stops active capture and speech. ## Is it ML, DL, or GenAI? **Primary classification: Deep Learning (DL), a subset of Machine Learning (ML).** The shipped visual recognition uses pretrained MediaPipe neural networks. Temporal confidence filtering and phrase mapping are deterministic application logic. The avatar is procedural animation. There is no LLM, generative translation model, or OpenAI API dependency. The long-term project remains **Deep Learning — SignBridge Accessibility Agent**, with ASL–English translation as a proposed future research direction. Actual language scope must be agreed with Deaf collaborators and sign-language specialists; seven hand categories do not establish support for a natural sign language. ## Try it locally Requirements: **Node.js 24**, npm, an internet connection for the initial dependency/model download, and a current desktop Chromium browser. Camera access requires HTTPS or localhost. Text input and captions remain available if optional speech APIs are unsupported. ```bash git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-SignBridge.git cd DL-SignBridge/app npm ci npm run assets npm run dev ``` Open the Local URL printed by Vite, normally `http://127.0.0.1:5173/`. No API key or account database is needed. Model and WASM assets are self-hosted after preparation; there is no service-worker/offline-install guarantee. ### Walk through both directions 1. Choose **Run sample photo**. Wait for the real model to propose **Yes**. 2. Edit the caption if needed, then choose **Speak caption**. Choose an installed voice under **Studio settings** if necessary. 3. To use a camera, choose **Enable camera**, review consent, then grant browser permission. Hold one supported gesture steady until a proposal appears. Review before speaking. 4. Switch to **Speech / text → Avatar**. Type **Peace** or select a phrase and choose **Animate message**. 5. Optionally choose **Use microphone**, review its separate privacy notice, dictate a supported phrase, and review the transcript before animating it. 6. Try an unsupported sentence: the app preserves the text and declines to invent a gesture. 7. Use **Clear session & stop devices** to stop camera, microphone, and speech and clear session content. ## Supported demo vocabulary | Model category | Demo phrase | Reverse-input aliases | | --- | --- | --- | | `Open_Palm` | Hello | hello, hi, open palm | | `Thumb_Up` | Yes | yes, thumb up, thumbs up | | `Thumb_Down` | No | no, thumb down, thumbs down | | `Closed_Fist` | Wait | wait, fist, closed fist | | `Pointing_Up` | One moment | one moment, point up, pointing up | | `Victory` | Peace | peace, victory | | `ILoveYou` | I love you | i love you | Matching is case-insensitive and ignores common punctuation; it requires the complete supported phrase. For example, “No thanks” is unsupported even though “No” is supported. Manual library previews are explicitly labeled and do not create camera-recognition results. ## Current architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD Camera[User-authorized camera] --> Frames[One in-flight image bitmap] Sample[Attributed sample photo] --> Worker Frames --> Worker[Browser worker: MediaPipe neural inference] Assets[Self-hosted model and WASM] --> Worker Worker --> Landmarks[Gesture category, landmarks and timing] Landmarks --> Gate[Category allowlist, confidence and camera hold] Gate --> Review[Editable caption proposal] Review --> Confirm[User chooses Speak caption] Confirm --> TTS[Browser text-to-speech] TTS --> Speaking[Decorative avatar mouth animation] Mic[Separately consented microphone] --> ASR[Optional browser speech provider] ASR --> Text[Editable English text] Typed[Typed phrase] --> Text Text --> Exact[Whole-phrase vocabulary matching] Exact --> Supported[Supported illustrative pose] Exact --> Fallback[Unsupported: visible text fallback] Supported --> Avatar[Three.js procedural avatar] ``` The model runs off the UI thread. Camera frames preserve their source aspect ratio for inference, with letterboxed preview and landmark alignment. Media tracks, worker resources, and avatar GPU resources have explicit cleanup paths. The 3D renderer loads separately from the initial interface bundle. ## Verify and build From `app/`: ```bash npm test npm run build npm audit --audit-level=moderate npx playwright install chromium npm run test:e2e npm run preview ``` Browser tests run against a dedicated local production-preview port. The sample test uses actual model inference. Physical audio output and microphone recognition are stubbed at their browser API boundaries in automated tests. A generated camera stream from the attributed sample exercises the actual frame loop and hold gate; this does not validate a physical camera or a real signer's performance. The test suite regenerates the README's five showcases. Dependency licenses and model provenance are documented in [third-party notices](app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [the model provenance manifest](app/public/models/provenance.json). See [evaluation protocol](docs/evaluation.md) for a private dataset harness and [production readiness](docs/production-readiness.md) for the remaining release gates. The GitHub workflow runs install, asset preparation, tests, build, audit, and browser checks on pushes and pull requests. Latest local verification: **17 unit tests and 6 browser tests passed**, production build passed, no violations in the tested initial accessibility scan, and zero known dependency vulnerabilities. Read the [verification report](docs/verification.md) for the exact tested boundaries and limitations. Hosted deployment succeeded on October 28, 2026. ## Roadmap and honest progress - [x] Build a responsive studio with camera permission, caption review, avatar controls, and text fallback. - [x] Integrate a pretrained seven-category gesture baseline and real-model functional sample. - [x] Filter camera proposals by confidence, hold time, and release before repeating. - [x] Connect reviewed captions to speech and a bounded speech/text-to-avatar pathway. - [x] Add a gesture library, privacy notices, session clearing, and reduced decorative motion. - [x] Add reproducible evaluation tooling, automated checks, CI, and actual product screenshots. - [ ] Confirm the target natural language pair and use cases with compensated Deaf collaborators. - [ ] Establish a consented, representative, signer-disjoint evaluation dataset and publish metrics. - [ ] Train or integrate language-specific recognition and translation models, including continuous signing and non-manual grammar. - [ ] Add linguist-reviewed motion clips and validate avatar comprehensibility with fluent signers. - [ ] Measure end-to-end conversational latency on named physical devices and browsers. - [ ] Complete physical hardware, assistive-technology, independent accessibility, security, and operational release reviews. - [ ] Explore constrained generative motion only after validated baselines exist. The completed baseline is gesture classification, not completion of the original ASL translation research goals. A successful test photograph does not establish generalization or translation accuracy. This demo should not be used as a substitute for a qualified interpreter in critical interactions. ## Repository layout ```text DL-SignBridge/ ├── app/ │ ├── src/ # React studio, camera/speech hooks, domain logic, avatar │ ├── public/ # Worker, sample photo, generated local model/WASM assets │ ├── scripts/ # Asset preparation, local model diagnostics, evaluation │ ├── tests/ # Browser integration and accessibility tests │ ├── .openai/hosting.json # Sites identity and static hosting configuration │ └── THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md ├── docs/ │ ├── showcase/ # Five real product screenshots │ ├── evaluation.md # Evaluation manifest and methodology │ ├── production-readiness.md # Safeguards and remaining release gates │ └── artwork.md # Original concept-art provenance └── .github/workflows/verify.yml ``` ## Contributing and research references Contributions from Deaf collaborators, linguists, accessibility practitioners, animators, and ML engineers are welcome. Open an issue with the language, use case, evidence, and expected outcome. Do not upload recordings, transcripts, or datasets without consent and redistribution rights. Private data, model caches, and local evaluation reports are excluded from Git. - [MediaPipe Gesture Recognizer documentation](https://ai.google.dev/edge/mediapipe/solutions/vision/gesture_recognizer/web_js) — model integration and supported categories. - [Sign Language Recognition, Generation, and Translation: An Interdisciplinary Perspective](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/wp-content/uploads/2019/07/Sign_Language_Workshop_Camera_accessible.pdf) — linguistic context and the distinction between recognition, translation, and production. - [U.S. Deaf Community Perspectives on Automatic Sign Language Translation](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/uploads/prod/2023/10/Automatic_Sign_Language_Translation_Perspectives.pdf) — community perspectives for participatory design. ## License No open-source license has been selected for original project code. Public visibility alone does not grant reuse rights. Third-party code, model weights, and sample assets retain their respective licenses; see [third-party notices](app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Screenshots show the implemented demo. The older cover image is AI-generated concept artwork.

Includes real-photo demo, product screenshots and end-to-end tests.
projects.readme: # DL – SugarLens **Private, on-device produce recognition with transparent sugar estimates. Web, mobile PWA, and Capacitor native packaging.** [Open the live demo](https://sugarlens-produce-vams2krish.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site) · [Source code](https://github.com/vams2krish/DL-SugarLens) · [Model and data limitations](#scope-and-limitations) The live deployment retains owner-only access; the GitHub source is public. Sign in with the owner's account to open the hosted app. ![SugarLens product overview: scanner, food insights, portion list and food library](docs/showcase-desktop.png) SugarLens identifies supported fruits and vegetables from a photo, asks you to confirm the match, and looks up average natural sugar content from USDA FoodData Central. It never claims to measure sugar or portion weight from pixels. The first roadmap release adds multiple object detection, 28 source-verified foods, weighted portion comparisons, CSV export, explicit offline model storage, and native packaging commands. ## Product showcases ### 1. Real photo → confirmation → sugar estimate The **Try a real photo demo** button runs the actual MobileNet model on the included banana photograph. After confirmation, entering 200 g produces an estimate of **24.40 g sugar**. No recognition responses are mocked or prerecorded. ![Actual banana photo recognition and reference sugar profile](docs/showcase-photo-scan.png) ### 2. More than one item in a photo COCO-SSD locates supported objects independently and draws numbered bounding boxes. Each match has its own confirmation button. This showcase uses two copies of the licensed demo photograph, with two real detections. ![Multi-item recognition with two separately detected bananas](docs/showcase-multiple-items.png) ### 3. Compare real portions and export your list Add a weighed portion of each confirmed food. A 200 g banana portion plus 100 g strawberry contains approximately **29.29 g total sugar** in 300 g food, or **9.76% by mass**. The total is a mass-weighted calculation, not a sum of food percentages. Download the actual rows as a CSV. ![Portion comparison with total grams, sugar and weighted percentage](docs/showcase-portions.png) ### 4. Save recognition for offline use Download both model weights to browser IndexedDB, check their saved status, or remove them. The production service worker precaches app code, bundled fonts, the food library and demo photo. Recognition loads the saved weights after a reload without contacting an inference server. ![Offline model download, check and removal controls](docs/showcase-offline.png) ### 5. The mobile experience The same features adapt to a narrow phone viewport. Camera capture and photo selection are separate controls. Add the PWA to your home screen through the browser menu. ## Is this ML, DL or Gen AI? **Deep Learning (DL), a subset of Machine Learning (ML).** MobileNet V2 performs single-image classification; COCO-SSD with a Lite MobileNet V2 backbone performs object detection. These are pretrained neural networks running through TensorFlow.js in the browser. This project uses inference, not a newly trained produce-specific model. It is not generative AI. Sugar estimates come from reviewed nutrition records and arithmetic. ## What shipped in version 1.1 | Roadmap area | Delivered behavior | | --- | --- | | Multiple foods | Numbered bounding boxes and independent confirmation for supported COCO-SSD produce classes | | Nutrition coverage | 28 raw produce records, each matched against saved USDA API snapshots | | Exploration | Search by food name, sort by sugar/name, show all/fewer foods | | Portion comparisons | Add/remove up to 100 portions, mass-weighted total, tab-session recovery and CSV export | | Offline recognition | Explicit model download, check and removal using versioned IndexedDB entries | | Offline app | Versioned service worker precache, local fonts, update prompt and offline connection indicator | | Product demo | Bundled, licensed real photograph; real inference; reproducible two-object E2E fixture | | Native delivery | Capacitor config plus reproducible Android/iOS preparation commands; Android generation/sync verified | | Verification | Unit tests, production-browser E2E checks, mobile layout and real-model inference checks | ## Run locally Use **Node.js 22.12+** and npm (Capacitor CLI requires Node 22+). ```bash npm ci npm run dev ``` For a production demo on your computer: ```bash npm run build npm run preview -- --port 4173 ``` Open `http://127.0.0.1:4173`. The first online visit precaches the shell. Click **Download models** before trying offline recognition. On a phone, open the HTTPS deployment; your computer's loopback URL does not point to the computer from another device. ## Repeatable end-to-end demo 1. Click **Try a real photo demo**. Wait for real inference, then confirm **Banana**. 2. Enter **200** in edible portion grams. Verify **24.40 g sugar**, then **Add portion to list**. 3. Choose **Strawberry**, leave 100 g, and add it. Verify the total **29.29 g sugar / 9.76%**. 4. Click **Download CSV** and inspect the two source-linked rows. 5. Select **Multiple items**, then **Scan in selected mode**. The detector draws a banana box. Upload your own photo containing supported objects to explore multiple matches. 6. Search **blue** in the library and select **Blueberry** for its USDA sugar profile. 7. Click **Download models**, wait until both say **yes**, reload, and check their status. 8. Disable network access and reload. Repeat the photo demo in both modes; manual food lookup and portions also remain available. 9. Remove saved models. Without network access, recognition explains the missing download while manual lookup continues working. Actual photographed food can be misidentified. Confirm every match and correct it manually before relying on reference values. ## Recognition and nutrition coverage **Single-produce mode:** ImageNet labels for Granny Smith/apple, banana, orange, strawberry, pineapple, lemon, broccoli, cucumber, cauliflower, bell pepper, zucchini/courgette and head cabbage. Suggestions require at least 10% model probability. The general apple reference is not variety-specific; bell pepper uses the red sweet pepper reference. **Multi-item mode:** apple, banana, orange, broccoli and carrot only, with a 50% score threshold and up to 20 objects per image. Other COCO classes are ignored. Detection boxes do not measure edible mass, reliably count obscured fruit, or segment the food. Thresholds are usability filters, not calibrated accuracy guarantees. **Manual library:** Apple, Banana, Orange, Strawberry, Pineapple, Lemon, Broccoli, Cucumber, Carrot, Tomato, Watermelon, Grapes, Avocado, Cauliflower, Red bell pepper, Zucchini, Cabbage, Mango, Blueberry, Raspberry, Pear, Peach, Plum, Kiwi, Spinach, Celery, Onion and Potato. Every record links to its USDA FDC ID. Reviewed snapshots are in [`docs/usda-reference-snapshot.json`](docs/usda-reference-snapshot.json) and [`docs/usda-roadmap-snapshot.json`](docs/usda-roadmap-snapshot.json), retrieved October 28, 2026. Tests assert that all bundled sugar values match these snapshots. ```text Photo → local MobileNet classification / COCO-SSD detection → user confirmation → USDA reference → user-entered edible grams → estimated sugar → optional portion list and CSV Food sugar % by mass = grams total sugar per 100 g food Portion sugar = food sugar per 100 g × edible portion grams ÷ 100 Combined sugar % = sum(portion sugar) ÷ sum(portion grams) × 100 ``` ## Offline use, privacy and updates The production build precaches its versioned app shell, JavaScript modules, local fonts, demo image and source-backed food table. Model weights are saved only after **Download models**. This uses roughly 40 MB for models plus app resources, depending on backend/version. Browser storage limits, private browsing and automatic eviction can prevent persistence. **Check saved models** before travelling; download success does not guarantee indefinite storage retention. Uploaded photos are decoded into an in-memory canvas, resized to a maximum 1,280 px edge for inference, and never uploaded or persisted. Inputs are limited to JPG/PNG/WebP, 12 MB, and 40 megapixels. Convert unsupported formats such as HEIC first. New or invalid uploads clear previous photo results. The portion list stores only food IDs and entered weights in `sessionStorage`; clear it explicitly or close the tab. No account database, photo history or analytics is included. Initial model downloads use TensorFlow/Google model hosting, which receives ordinary network metadata. Font files are bundled locally. Online navigation refreshes through the host so its authentication redirects remain valid; offline navigation reconstructs the saved shell response without redirect or compression metadata. A dedicated service-worker regression test covers this hosted reload path. New app versions show an update action; activating it preserves the current tab's portion list. Model removal clears the saved recognition weights without deleting food data or the app shell. ## Mobile and native packaging The deployed version is an **installable PWA**, not a signed app-store binary. iPhone Safari: **Share → Add to Home Screen**. Android Chrome: **Install app / Add to Home screen**. The in-app install button opens the browser install prompt where available, otherwise it displays instructions. Capacitor packaging shares the production `dist/` implementation: ```bash npm run native:android npx cap open android # Run on a Mac with Xcode for iOS development npm run native:ios npx cap open ios ``` The preparation commands create the platform folder if needed and sync the current web build. Generated platform folders are ignored so they can be recreated. Android source generation and sync were verified on Windows. Building/signing Android requires Android Studio and the Android SDK; iOS builds/signing require macOS and Xcode. Camera chooser behavior and offline storage must be validated on physical target devices before store submission. No APK, AAB, IPA or store release is claimed in this version. ## Verification and delivery ```bash npm test npm run build npm run preview -- --port 4173 # Keep running in a separate terminal npm run test:e2e ``` E2E uses local Microsoft Edge through Playwright. In CI it uses Playwright Chromium (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`). It tests the actual production build and real models, not mocked predictions. It covers photo confirmation, two-object detection, portion arithmetic and CSV bytes, nutrition search, offline model persistence/reload, invalid image recovery, mobile overflow, removal and missing-model fallback. It also captures the README showcases and writes an inspectable result to [`docs/verification.json`](docs/verification.json). The automated demo is a small curated regression test, not a statistically meaningful accuracy benchmark. It cannot replace diverse camera testing, accessibility review or physical-device validation. Dependency audits check known advisories at the time they run; they are not a security certification. ```text src/main.js Product interface, camera/upload flow, food library and portions src/inference.js Lazy model loading, IndexedDB persistence and removal src/foods.js USDA references and supported recognition mappings src/portions.js Weighted calculations and CSV serialization src/style.css Responsive visual design and keyboard focus states scripts/prepare-sw.mjs Build-specific precache generation scripts/native.mjs Reproducible native source preparation scripts/verify.mjs Production E2E flow and actual product screenshots public/demo/ Licensed photograph and attribution docs/ Product showcases, source snapshots and verification evidence ``` ## Scope and limitations Reference values describe raw edible produce, not juice, dried fruit, mixed recipes, cooked food or added sugars. Ripeness, cultivar, storage and preparation affect actual sugar. The app does not measure Brix or laboratory sugar concentration and is not intended for medical dosing or treatment decisions. Weights must be supplied by the user. The general-purpose pretrained models have narrow supported produce labels and can misidentify unusual lighting, sliced food, crowded scenes and unsupported varieties. No custom model has been trained and no held-out produce benchmark is claimed. CPU-only inference may be slower on older phones. ## Next roadmap | Next step | What is needed | | --- | --- | | Dedicated produce classifier | Licensed diverse dataset, train/validation/test separation, held-out class-level metrics and model export | | Broader multi-food recognition | Produce-specific detection data, bounding-box labels and evaluation beyond the five supported COCO food classes | | Physical mobile certification | Android/iOS camera, memory, offline persistence, install/update and accessibility checks on target devices | | Signed native releases | Platform SDKs, signing identities, final app identifiers, icons and store submissions | | Nutrition expansion | Further reviewed raw/cooked/variety-specific records with explicit preparation selection | ## Sources and licenses - [USDA FoodData Central](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/) and [data documentation](https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/data-documentation.html). - [MobileNet model documentation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/tree/master/mobilenet) and [COCO-SSD documentation](https://github.com/tensorflow/tfjs-models/tree/master/coco-ssd). - [TensorFlow.js model storage documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/js/guide/save_load). - [Capacitor documentation](https://capacitorjs.com/docs). - Demo photo: [Banana-Single.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Banana-Single.jpg), **Evan-Amos**, [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/). The original photo is bundled unchanged. The two-photo demo montage and screenshot regions incorporating the photo retain CC BY-SA 3.0. No endorsement is implied. - Application code: MIT. Dependencies, model weights and fonts retain their respective licenses. Product showcases are screenshots of the actual application.

projects.readme:
# 💨 Fart Alert

### Step away. Let it rip.

A playful desktop app that turns computer inactivity into a questionable soundtrack. Fart Alert detects system-wide mouse and keyboard inactivity, plays random fart sounds when you step away, and stops playback when you return.

Built with **Electron, React, Vite, Web Audio, and Framer Motion**. Settings and custom sounds stay on your device.

![Fart Alert desktop app with animated cloud mascot, inactivity monitor, theme settings, frequency controls, and custom sound uploader](docs/images/fart-alert-desktop.png)

## Features

- **System-wide inactivity detection:** mouse and keyboard activity anywhere on your computer resets the idle timer, including while the app is minimized.
- **Automatic playback and stop:** repeat random sounds while idle; stop when activity resumes. Activity is checked approximately every 250 ms.
- **Configurable timeout:** 5 seconds to 2 minutes, with a 10-second default.
- **Three sound themes:** Cartoon Chaos, Heavy Duty, and Musical Farts.
- **Frequency and volume controls:** Gentle, Standard, or Extreme, plus a sound test button.
- **Custom WAV/MP3 uploads:** preview, enable, disable, and delete individual sounds.
- **Playful visuals:** animated cloud mascot, colorful particle bursts, idle progress, and a session fart counter.
- **Local persistence:** settings and uploaded sounds survive restarts. Monitoring starts paused on every launch.

## Quick start

### Requirements

- Node.js **22.12 or later** and npm; initially built and tested with Node.js 24.
- Windows for the included portable packaging script and desktop test setup.
- An audio output device with its volume turned up.
- Internet access for the initial dependency and Electron runtime downloads.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FartAlert.git
cd FartAlert
npm ci
npm run build
npm start
```

1. Click **Test sound** to check your audio.
2. Choose your timeout, sound personality, frequency, and volume.
3. Click **Activate Fart Alert**.
4. Stop using the mouse and keyboard and wait for the timeout.
5. Move the mouse or press a key to stop the idle playback.

Click **Pause Fart Alert** to disable monitoring. Minimizing the window keeps monitoring active; closing it quits the app. The app does not prevent sleep, so sleeping the computer suspends it.

## Custom sounds: upload → active → idle playback

**Uploading a valid sound automatically enables it.** No second selection is needed.

Choose one or more `.wav` or `.mp3` files in **Your secret weapons**. Each file must be **15 MB or less** and successfully decode as audio. Accepted files appear with their enabled toggle checked.

| Control or state | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Play icon beside a file | Preview that specific sound |
| Checked toggle | Include the file in random idle playback |
| Disabled toggle | Keep the file saved but exclude it from idle playback |
| Trash icon | Remove the saved sound |
| One or more custom sounds enabled | Randomly choose from those files instead of the built-in theme |
| All custom sounds disabled | Use the selected built-in theme again |

Random selection can repeat the same file. Previewing a file does not change its enabled state. Uploading a sound does not activate monitoring if monitoring is paused.

Files are stored locally in IndexedDB. There is no server upload, account requirement, or cloud synchronization. Clearing the app's local data removes saved files and settings.

## Sound themes and frequency

| Theme | Personality |
| --- | --- |
| Cartoon Chaos | Wobbly, bubbly synthesized toots |
| Heavy Duty | Lower-pitched, longer rumbles |
| Musical Farts | A short sequence of musical pitches |

Built-in sounds are generated locally with Web Audio. Enabled custom files override the selected theme.

| Frequency | Approximate start-to-start interval |
| --- | --- |
| Gentle | 9 seconds |
| Standard | 4 seconds |
| Extreme | 1.2 seconds |

Timing varies slightly at random. Longer sounds finish before the next idle sound starts, with a short gap. Volume changes apply to the next sound. Zero volume silences playback without pausing monitoring.

## Development commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | Install locked dependencies |
| `npm run dev` | Run Vite and Electron together |
| `npm run build` | Build the production renderer into `dist/` |
| `npm start` | Open the desktop app using the production build |
| `npm run preview` | Serve the built UI in a browser |
| `npm test` | Run Electron end-to-end tests |
| `npm run package` | Build a portable Windows app |

**Browser limitation:** browser preview monitors activity inside its page only. Use Electron for inactivity detection across your computer.

## Build a Windows desktop app

```powershell
npm run package
```

Open `release/Fart Alert/Fart Alert.exe`. Keep the entire generated folder together: the executable needs its accompanying runtime files. This is a portable folder build, not an installer.

Generated dependencies, runtimes, caches, and build output are excluded from Git. This repository contains source code; build the executable locally unless a separate release is published. The packaging script currently targets Windows. macOS and Linux packages have not been configured or verified.

## Architecture and privacy

1. Electron's main process reads operating-system idle duration with `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`.
2. An isolated preload bridge exposes that reading to the renderer through IPC.
3. The renderer checks the duration approximately every 250 ms against the configured timeout.
4. While idle and activated, it selects an enabled custom sound or synthesizes the chosen theme.
5. Framer Motion particles and the mascot respond to playback; further sounds follow the frequency setting.
6. Returning activity cancels pending playback and stops the current sound.

The app reads elapsed inactivity. It does not record typed keys, inspect other applications, capture screenshots, or save mouse trails. Node integration is disabled in the renderer and context isolation is enabled. There is no application backend, analytics service, or API key configuration.

```text
electron/
  main.cjs             Desktop window and system idle API
  preload.cjs          Isolated IPC bridge
src/
  main.jsx             Monitoring, settings, uploads, UI, particles
  audio.js             Web Audio synthesis and custom playback
  storage.js           IndexedDB sound persistence
  style.css            Responsive earthy visual design
scripts/package.mjs    Portable Windows packaging
tests/desktop.mjs      Electron end-to-end checks
docs/images/           Project screenshots
vite.config.js         Renderer development and build settings
```

## Verification

The production build and Electron tests passed during initial implementation, including the packaged app. Tests check the real desktop idle API, upload auto-enabling, repeated custom playback during simulated idle time, stopping on simulated return, persistence after reload, theme fallback, preview, invalid files, deletion, and renderer errors.

Tests use controlled idle readings after checking the native API. They do not physically move the mouse or verify speaker output. For a manual test, activate the app, step away until it plays, then use the mouse or keyboard in another application.

After packaging, run:

```powershell
node tests/desktop.mjs --packaged
```

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| No sound | Try **Test sound**, increase app and system volume, and check the audio output device. |
| No idle playback | Activate monitoring, then wait without using the computer. Use the desktop edition. |
| Theme is ignored | Disable all custom sounds; enabled uploads take priority. |
| File is rejected | Choose a decodable WAV or MP3 of 15 MB or less. |
| App will not start after cloning | Run `npm ci`, `npm run build`, then `npm start`. |
| Portable executable fails | Keep its accompanying runtime files in the generated folder. |
| Electron download runs out of space | Free disk space or put temporary files and the Electron download cache on a drive with space. |

## Contributing

Issues and pull requests are welcome. Include reproduction steps, operating system, selected theme and frequency, and whether custom sounds are enabled. Run the production build and relevant desktop tests before submitting playback changes.

## License

[ISC](LICENSE). Third-party packages retain their respective licenses.

---

*Stay curious. Stay hydrated. Stay upwind.*

# FlirtLive

**Find your people. Feel the connection.**

FlirtLive is a premium live social streaming **front-end prototype** for an adults-only community. It combines creator discovery, a live room interface, local chat, virtual gifts, a demo coin wallet, follows, leaderboards, and profile editing in a responsive dark navy interface with purple and pink accents.

![FlirtLive home page showing the featured host, discovery filters, and host grid](flirtlive-home.png)

## Project showcase

The home screenshot above is an actual capture from the initial demo build. Additional live-room, discovery, leaderboard, wallet, profile, and mobile captures are pending browser access; no generated mockups are presented as tested application screenshots.

## Project status

This is an interactive browser demo, not an operational webcam service. Host identities, viewer counts, rankings, messages, and stream status are sample data. Room backgrounds are still portraits, not live video. The pictured models are stock-photo subjects and are not represented as actual platform hosts. No explicit content is included.

The private hosted preview is available to its owner at [FlirtLive preview](https://flirtlive-social-lounge.adam-vamshikrishna.chatgpt.site). Public repository access does not grant access to that private preview.

## Features

| Area | Current experience |
| --- | --- |
| Home | Featured hero, host cards, live badges, country labels, categories, and sample viewer counts |
| Discover | Search hosts by name, country, and interests; category and country filtering |
| Live room | Portrait stage, host information, follow action, share action, and local chat composition |
| Virtual gifts | Rose, Love, Diamond, Teddy Bear, Crown, and Rocket; sending deducts demo coins |
| Coin wallet | Starting balance of 1,250 test coins; simulated package top-ups without payment |
| Following | Follow/unfollow hosts and browse saved favorites |
| Top Live | Sample weekly rankings and a top-three podium |
| Messages | Sample creator invitations linking to their rooms; not private messaging |
| Profile | Editable display name and bio, local profile-photo upload, following and gifting stats |
| Host onboarding | Interest dialog saved on the current device; no camera capture or broadcast |
| Responsive UI | Sidebar navigation, mobile layouts, gradients, translucent panels, and hover transitions |

## Run locally

No package installation, API key, or build step is required. Install Python 3 and serve the static files:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FlirtLive.git
cd FlirtLive
python -m http.server 4173 --directory dist
```

Open [http://localhost:4173](http://localhost:4173). Stop the server with `Ctrl+C`.

Alternatively, use any static HTTP server with `dist/` as the document root. Deploy that same directory to a static hosting provider.

## Pages and routes

| Route | Page |
| --- | --- |
| `#home` | Featured content and live host grid |
| `#discover` | Host browser |
| `#room/1` | Example host room; IDs 1–8 are available |
| `#following` | Saved follows |
| `#top` | Leaderboard |
| `#coins` | Demo wallet and gift catalog |
| `#messages` | Sample invitations |
| `#profile` | Profile editor |

Navigation uses URL hashes, so a static server needs no route rewrites. Press `Ctrl+K` or `Cmd+K` to focus search.

## Technology and structure

- Semantic HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript; no application framework or build dependencies.
- CSS Grid/Flexbox, responsive media queries, and Google Fonts (DM Sans and Manrope).
- Sample portraits loaded from Unsplash image URLs.
- Browser `localStorage` for demo preferences and wallet/profile state.

```text
FlirtLive/
├── dist/
│   ├── index.html          # Application shell and navigation
│   ├── style.css           # Theme, components, and responsive styles
│   └── app.js              # Demo data, routing, rendering, and interactions
├── flirtlive-home.png       # Project screenshot


├── .gitignore
└── README.md
```

## Data behavior and limitations

The `flirtlive` localStorage entry stores the coin balance, following list, profile name/bio/avatar, and coins gifted. The separate `hostInterest` entry stores hosting interest. These values belong to one browser on one device; they are not synchronized, authenticated, or tamper-resistant. Clear those entries to reset the demo. Room chat messages and gift notifications persist locally, with up to 100 entries per room. They are not shared with other users. Do not use the demo for sensitive information or real monetary balances.

Photo uploads accept image files up to 2 MB and store them locally. Large images can exceed browser storage quotas. External images and fonts require an internet connection. Profile XP and level indicators are illustrative, not a progression engine.

## Production roadmap

To turn this interface into an operational platform, the remaining work includes:

1. Authentication, account recovery, persistent user profiles, and authorization.
2. A real streaming provider/WebRTC implementation, host publishing, viewer playback, and presence.
3. Shared room chat and private messaging with server persistence and abuse controls.
4. Server-authoritative wallet accounting, payment processing, gift transactions, refunds, and creator payouts.
5. Age and creator identity verification, consent workflows, moderation, reporting/blocking, and operational policies appropriate to the intended service.
6. Real discovery, rankings, follow counts, media storage, analytics, and administration.
7. Automated tests, accessibility review, performance work, deployment configuration, monitoring, and security review.

The current browser demo has no backend, database, payment integration, streaming service, or real age-verification mechanism. An “18+” label is not verification.

## Validation

Run `node --check dist/app.js` and `node --test tests/demo.test.cjs`. Five regression tests cover routes/discovery, wallet/gifts, chat/follow persistence, profile saving, and storage recovery using a simulated DOM. See [the verification report](docs/VERIFICATION.md) for evidence and limits. Fresh live browser verification and additional page screenshots are pending because browser use is disabled in Work settings.

## Images and licensing

The screenshot documents this project's interface. Portrait imagery is loaded from Unsplash; the source image identifiers are listed in `dist/app.js`. Review the applicable image terms and replace placeholder assets before production use. Third-party imagery and fonts retain their respective rights. No open-source software license has been selected for this repository.

# PDRides — Full-Stack Ride-Sharing Application

**Public-Demand Ride-share Made Easy**

PDRides is a community ride-sharing web application that connects passengers and drivers through a browser interface and messaging integrations. The project brings together ride discovery, driver ride offers, seat booking, route planning, estimated fares, account settings, and advertising configuration. Its product goal is a platform with no platform fees for passengers or drivers.

![PDRides project screenshot showing the home page and messaging entry points](docs/images/pdrides-home.png)

*Actual project home page captured locally. Marketing statements displayed in the interface are product copy, not independently verified usage or service guarantees.*

[Source code](https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides/issues)

## Product showcase

Actual locally rendered project screens. These show the interface; successful production authentication and bookings have not been verified.

### Passenger and driver login

![Passenger and driver role selection](docs/images/pdrides-login.png)

Role selection before phone verification.

### Registration

![Multi-step passenger and driver registration](docs/images/pdrides-register.png)

Personal information, contact details, and preferences. OTP delivery and persisted registration require a working database.

### Map and trip planning

![OpenStreetMap tiles, pickup and destination, and fare controls](docs/images/pdrides-map.png)

Map tiles render successfully. Location access was unavailable, as shown in the screenshot. Fare calculation and bookings were not verified.

### Help center

![Help center topics and frequently asked questions](docs/images/pdrides-help.png)

Support topics for accounts, rides, payments, safety, and technical questions.

## Live verification status

**Production end-to-end verification is blocked:** the configured MongoDB connection returned `MongooseServerSelectionError`, and no deployed demo homepage URL is configured in GitHub. Six local preview pages returned HTTP 200 and 26 backend JavaScript modules passed syntax checks. Screenshots were visually inspected. The preview returns HTTP 503 for APIs and does not simulate successful accounts, rides, or bookings.

Read the [verification report](docs/verification-2026-10-29.md) for evidence, production blockers, and remaining acceptance steps. No real messages, production bookings, or account changes were performed.

## Project overview

Drivers can publish trips with pickup and destination details, timing, available seats, and a contribution amount. Passengers can discover rides and use booking flows. Map services supply location search, routing, distance, and fare estimates. WhatsApp supports messaging and phone verification; Telegram webhook and bot service modules are also included. MongoDB stores users, rides, conversations, and advertisements.

This repository is an application prototype with implemented backend routes and frontend screens. Messaging requires configured provider accounts, and the instant booking flow currently assigns a mock driver. A screenshot or a successful server start does not establish that all integrations are working in production.

## Features and implementation

| Area | Included in the codebase |
| --- | --- |
| Ride discovery | Browse rides, filter by trip details, view shared ride pages, and see seat availability |
| Driver tools | Publish and manage ride offers with vehicle/profile information |
| Passenger tools | Book seats, cancel bookings, and review ride history |
| Maps | Leaflet interface, OpenStreetMap tiles, Nominatim location lookup, and OSRM routing |
| Fare estimates | Distance/time calculations, ride-type pricing, and detailed fare breakdowns |
| Accounts | WhatsApp OTP flows, registration, sessions, profile and driver settings |
| Preferences | Favorite routes, recent searches, privacy and notification settings |
| Messaging | WhatsApp Cloud API service/webhook and Telegram bot service/webhook |
| Advertising | Ad models, API routes, placement configuration, geographic targeting, and fallback content |
| Maintenance | Scheduled ride expiration and completion tasks; application/database health routes |

## Technology

- **Frontend:** HTML, CSS, browser JavaScript, and Leaflet.
- **Backend:** Node.js with ECMAScript modules and Express 4.
- **Persistence:** MongoDB, Mongoose 8, and the MongoDB Node.js driver 7.
- **Integrations:** WhatsApp Cloud API, Telegram Bot API, Nominatim, and OSRM.
- **Utilities:** Axios, dotenv, node-cron, and nodemon for development.

## Local setup

### Prerequisites

- Node.js **20.19 or newer**, matching the minimum required by the declared MongoDB 7 driver dependency.
- npm and a reachable MongoDB instance, locally or hosted.
- A Meta WhatsApp Cloud API application for WhatsApp delivery and OTP testing.
- A Telegram bot token if testing Telegram integration.

### Install and configure

```bash
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/FullStack-PDRides.git
cd FullStack-PDRides
npm install
```

Copy the environment template:

```powershell
# PowerShell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
```

```bash
# macOS / Linux
cp .env.example .env
```

Edit `.env` with your own configuration. Use the same port in `PORT` and `WEB_APP_URL`; the template currently has different values. A consistent local example is:

```dotenv
PORT=3000
NODE_ENV=development
APP_NAME=PDRides
MONGODB_URI=mongodb://localhost:27017/pdrides
WEB_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID=your_phone_number_id
WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_access_token
WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN=your_verification_token
TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your_bot_token
TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET=your_webhook_secret
MAX_RIDE_RESULTS=5
```

| Variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PORT` | HTTP port; the server falls back to `3002` when unset |
| `MONGODB_URI` | Database connection; `MONGO_URI` and `MONGODB_URL` are fallback aliases |
| `MONGODB_DATABASE` | Optional database name; defaults to `pdrides` |
| `WEB_APP_URL` | Base URL used for links sent in messages |
| `APP_NAME` | Optional display name in server/health output |
| `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` | Your Meta WhatsApp phone-number resource ID |
| `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN` | Credential for WhatsApp message delivery |
| `WHATSAPP_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` | Value used during webhook verification |
| `WHATSAPP_API_VERSION` | Optional Graph API version override used by the WhatsApp service |
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | Telegram bot credential |
| `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Telegram webhook configuration secret |
| `MAX_RIDE_RESULTS` | Ride-result configuration from the environment template |

The template also contains `MAPBOX_TOKEN` and `OPENROUTESERVICE_KEY`; the current map service uses Nominatim and OSRM directly. Keep `.env` private and replace the example phone-number ID with your own.

Some integration modules read environment variables during module initialization. If credentials from `.env` are not picked up with `npm start`, preload the file before importing the app:

```bash
node --env-file=.env src/index.js
```

### Run

```bash
npm run dev
# or
npm start
```

The backend connects to MongoDB before opening its HTTP listener. With the configuration above, visit `http://localhost:3000/`.

## Screens and routes

| URL | Screen |
| --- | --- |
| `/` | Home page |
| `/map` | Interactive map and trip planning |
| `/register` | Registration |
| `/login` | Login |
| `/browse-all-rides` | Ride discovery |
| `/my-rides` | Personal rides |
| `/ride/:id` | Shareable ride details |
| `/settings` | Account and preferences |
| `/ads-config` | Advertising configuration interface |
| `/help-center` | Help content |
| `/contact-us` | Contact page |
| `/privacy-policy` | Privacy policy |
| `/terms-of-service` | Terms of service |

The static HTML files are also present at the repository root. Opening only those files does not supply the API or database functionality.

## API overview

| Endpoint or group | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /health` | Application liveness |
| `GET /api/health`, `GET /api/ping` | Database-aware health and connectivity |
| `/api/auth/*` | OTP requests, verification, registration, and session operations |
| `/api/user/*` | Profile, vehicle details, preferences, and history |
| `/api/users/me/*` | Unified current-user profile and preferences routes |
| `GET /api/rides`, `POST /api/rides` | Search and create ride offers |
| `/api/rides/:id/*` | Ride booking, cancellation, completion, and status operations |
| `GET /api/fare` | Fare estimates for pickup/destination locations |
| `POST /api/ride/book` | Prototype instant booking with a mock driver |
| `GET /api/route` | Route details |
| `GET /api/autocomplete`, `GET /api/reverse-geocode` | Location lookup |
| `/api/ads*` | Advertisement management and delivery routes |
| `/webhook` | WhatsApp verification and incoming events |
| `/telegram-webhook` | Telegram incoming events |

Consult [the app entry point](src/index.js) and [route modules](src/routes) for request fields and authorization behavior. Some ride and location routes are defined in the entry point before the unified API router; Express handles the first matching route, so overlapping handlers need to be considered when extending the API.

## Messaging setup

**WhatsApp:** Configure your own Meta credentials and verification token, expose the app through an HTTPS URL, and configure the callback at `/webhook`. Subscribe the provider application to the events needed by the webhook handlers. OTP and outgoing-message flows require working provider credentials.

**Telegram:** Configure your own bot token and webhook settings. [set-telegram-webhook.js](set-telegram-webhook.js) is the repository's setup helper; inspect its configuration before running it against a bot. The source includes both Telegram and WhatsApp integrations, but their presence does not confirm a deployed bot is online.

## Repository layout

```text
FullStack-PDRides/
├── index.html                 # Landing page
├── map-view.html              # Map and trip planning UI
├── browse-rides.html           # Ride discovery UI
├── my-rides.html               # Personal ride UI
├── ride-details.html           # Shared ride UI
├── login.html / register.html  # Account entry screens
├── settings.html               # User preferences
├── ads-config.html             # Advertising UI
├── css/                        # Screen styles
├── src/
│   ├── index.js                # Express app, routes, startup
│   ├── middleware/             # Authentication helpers
│   ├── models/                 # User, Ride, Conversation, Ad
│   ├── routes/                 # Auth, user, API, messaging, ads
│   └── services/               # Database, rides, maps, messaging, scheduling
├── ads-config/                 # Placement, targeting, unit and fallback JSON
├── ads-system/                 # Ad loader and developer configuration
├── docs/images/                # README project screenshot
├── test-*.js / test-*.json      # Manual integration scripts and sample payloads
├── .env.example                # Environment template
└── package.json                # Dependencies and commands
```

## Verification and current limitations

`npm test` is currently a placeholder that exits with an error; there is no automated test suite configured. The `test-*.js` scripts and `test-bot.html` are manual integration aids. Review their endpoints and payloads before running them, since some can send messages or modify records.

For a configured local instance:

```bash
curl http://localhost:3000/health
curl http://localhost:3000/api/health
```

Then exercise registration, an offered ride, ride discovery, booking/cancellation, and the messaging callbacks with test accounts.

Before production use, review authentication and authorization across all routes, OTP handling, CORS, input validation, provider webhook verification, and static file exposure. The app currently serves the repository root as static content, includes permissive demo CORS, and contains mock instant-booking behavior. These are implementation limitations rather than production service guarantees. Advertised live tracking, driver verification, reviews, and user-count claims should be validated against a complete deployed flow before being represented as operational capabilities.

## Contributing

Open an issue with reproduction steps or a proposed improvement. For code changes, describe the affected flow, configuration needs, and how it was verified. Do not include credentials, personal ride data, or production message payloads.

## License

`package.json` declares MIT, but this repository currently has no standalone `LICENSE` file. Confirm the intended license terms with the repository owner before relying on a license grant.

projects.readme:
# GenAI Game Industry Research Agents

![CrewAI project overview: researcher, writer, and Markdown article](docs/project-overview.svg)

A Python experiment that coordinates a **Senior Researcher** and a **Writer** with CrewAI. The crew searches the web through Serper, investigates technology trends in the games industry, and turns its findings into a Markdown article.

## Project summary

This repository demonstrates role-based agents, tool use, sequential tasks, memory, and caching in one readable script. It is a learning prototype rather than a deployed application. The project image above is an architecture illustration, not a screenshot of a user interface.

## How the workflow works

1. The researcher searches for games-industry trends and evaluates benefits, market opportunities, and risks.
2. The research task requests a three-paragraph report.
3. The writer runs after the researcher in a sequential crew and writes an accessible four-paragraph article.
4. CrewAI saves the article to `new-blog-post2.md`, and the script prints the final result.

| Component | Configuration in the script |
| --- | --- |
| Senior Researcher | Web search, verbose logging, memory, delegation enabled |
| Writer | Web search, verbose logging, memory, delegation disabled |
| Search tool | `SerperDevTool` |
| Execution | `Process.sequential` |
| Crew settings | Memory and caching enabled; `max_rpm=100` |
| Output | Markdown file plus terminal output |

## Repository contents

```text
app.py                       Agent definitions, tasks, crew, and execution
requirements.txt             Python dependencies (unpinned)
.env.example                 Placeholder environment variable names
.gitignore                   Excludes secrets, caches, and generated output
new-blog-post.md              Historical sample output from a different topic
README.md                    Project documentation
docs/project-overview.svg    Project architecture image
```

The historical `new-blog-post.md` discusses a different industry and contains unverified claims. It is retained as an existing artifact and is not representative of the current games-industry prompts or a validated research result.

## Setup

Use a Python version supported by your installed CrewAI release. See the [official CrewAI installation guide](https://docs.crewai.com/en/installation) for current requirements.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/vams2krish/GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents.git
cd GenAI-Game-Industry-Research-Agents
python -m venv .venv
.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

On macOS/Linux, activate the environment with `source .venv/bin/activate`.

### Credentials

The script reads two environment variables. Set them in the terminal where you run the project:

```powershell
$env:OPENAI_API_KEY = "YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY"
$env:SERPER_API_KEY = "YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
python app.py
```

For macOS/Linux:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY="YOUR_OPENAI_API_KEY"
export SERPER_API_KEY="YOUR_SERPER_API_KEY"
python app.py
```

`.env.example` is a reference only: the script does not automatically load `.env` files. Never put real credentials in source control. Missing credentials cause a clear error before the crew is constructed. Obtain credentials from [OpenAI Platform](https://platform.openai.com/) and [Serper](https://serper.dev/). Running the crew makes external API calls and may incur charges.

## Customizing the crew

Edit the agent `role`, `goal`, and `backstory` fields to change responsibilities. Adjust each task's `description` and `expected_output` to control the research scope and article structure. Change `output_file` to choose a different destination.

The `topic` passed to `crew.kickoff()` is currently not referenced through a `{topic}` placeholder in the task descriptions. Changing that input alone will not retarget the hardcoded games-industry prompts; edit the prompts as well. The research task's expected output mentions AI trends, while its description covers games-industry trends more broadly.

## Limitations and validation

- This is an older CrewAI example. Dependencies are unpinned, and compatibility with current releases has not been established. Settings such as `share_crew=True` may require review against the installed version.
- No model is explicitly selected in the script; model behavior and access depend on CrewAI configuration and provider defaults.
- Memory may require additional provider configuration and local storage, depending on the installed release.
- Search results and generated claims need human verification. The script does not enforce citations or fact-check its output.
- Verbose logs can contain prompts, research, and generated text. Review the configured sharing and logging behavior before processing private information.
- Publication checks cover Python syntax, repository contents, and credential removal. A live paid API run has not been performed.

## Suggested next steps
